skill_title: Apply Le Chatelier's Principle and explain industrial processes
notes: 20 items: 8 lifted, 12 fresh. Le Chatelier's principle (concentration, pressure, temperature, catalyst); industrial Haber, Contact, Ostwald processes.

items.question: State LE CHATELIER'S PRINCIPLE.
items.expectedAnswer: When the equilibrium of a system is disturbed by a change in conditions (concentration, pressure, temperature), the system will shift to oppose the change and re-establish equilibrium.
items.explanation: Two marks: 'system shifts' + 'to oppose the change'. Standard CAPS wording.

items.question: The equilibrium 2CrO₄²⁻ (yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) + H₂O is observed. Adding ACID to the solution causes the colour to change from yellow to orange. Explain.
items.expectedAnswer: Adding acid increases [H⁺]. By Le Chatelier, the equilibrium shifts to oppose the increase, i.e. shifts to the RIGHT (forward direction) to use up H⁺. This produces more Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange), so the solution turns orange.
items.explanation: Add reactant ⇒ equilibrium shifts AWAY (toward products) to consume it.

items.question: NaOH is added to the equilibrium 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O. Which is CORRECT?
items.expectedAnswer: [H⁺] decreases; equilibrium shifts left (more yellow)
items.explanation: NaOH provides OH⁻ which neutralises H⁺. So [H⁺] decreases. Equilibrium shifts LEFT to produce more H⁺, producing more CrO₄²⁻ (yellow).

items.question: How does INCREASING the temperature affect an EXOTHERMIC equilibrium reaction?
items.expectedAnswer: Increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the ENDOTHERMIC direction (the reverse direction for an exothermic forward reaction). The system absorbs the added heat by favouring the reverse reaction. So [products] decrease and Kc DECREASES.
items.explanation: Heat acts like a 'reactant' for exothermic. Add heat ⇒ system absorbs it ⇒ favours endothermic direction.

items.question: For the exothermic reaction H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI (ΔH < 0). On a concentration-time graph, [HI] suddenly DECREASES at t₂. Was the system HEATED or COOLED?
items.expectedAnswer: HEATED. For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing temperature favours the REVERSE (endothermic) direction. Reverse direction consumes HI ⇒ [HI] decreases. So the system was heated.
items.explanation: Exothermic forward ⇒ endothermic reverse. Heat ⇒ reverse favoured ⇒ HI consumed.

items.question: For 2HI(g) ⇌ H₂(g) + I₂(g): Kc at 721 K = 0.02 and at 850 K = 0.09. Is the forward reaction EXOTHERMIC or ENDOTHERMIC?
items.expectedAnswer: ENDOTHERMIC. Kc increases with increasing T. By Le Chatelier, increasing T favours the endothermic direction; if Kc increases (more products), the FORWARD direction must be endothermic.
items.explanation: T ↑, Kc ↑ ⇒ forward is endothermic. T ↑, Kc ↓ ⇒ forward is exothermic.

items.question: The reaction 3H₂(g) + N₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) is exothermic. Which condition INCREASES Kc?
items.expectedAnswer: Decrease temperature
items.explanation: Kc changes ONLY with temperature. For exothermic forward, decreasing T shifts equilibrium toward more products, so Kc increases. Pressure and catalyst do not change Kc.

items.question: How does INCREASING the PRESSURE affect the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)?
items.expectedAnswer: Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward the side with FEWER moles of gas. Reactants: 1 + 3 = 4 mol of gas. Products: 2 mol of gas. So equilibrium shifts to the RIGHT (products, NH₃), reducing the total moles of gas to oppose the pressure increase.
items.explanation: More pressure ⇒ shift to fewer gas moles. Haber reaction: 4 mol → 2 mol ⇒ pressure favours products.

items.question: Does adding a CATALYST shift the position of an equilibrium?
items.expectedAnswer: NO. A catalyst speeds up BOTH the forward and reverse reactions equally. The system reaches equilibrium FASTER, but at the SAME position (same Kc, same equilibrium concentrations). The catalyst does not change the equilibrium position.
items.explanation: Catalyst: kinetic effect (rate ↑) but no thermodynamic effect (position unchanged). Kc unchanged.

items.question: Describe the conditions used in the HABER process for producing ammonia (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, exothermic).
items.expectedAnswer: Haber process conditions: temperature ~400–500°C (a COMPROMISE — lower T gives higher equilibrium yield but slower rate; ~450°C is fast enough), pressure ~150–200 atm (HIGH — favours fewer-mole side, i.e. NH₃), iron (Fe) catalyst (with promoters) to speed equilibrium. NH₃ is removed to drive forward reaction.
items.explanation: Standard CAPS Haber conditions: high P, moderate T, Fe catalyst. T is a kinetics/yield compromise.

items.question: Describe the CONTACT process (sulfuric acid manufacture) in outline.
items.expectedAnswer: Three main steps: (1) S + O₂ → SO₂; (2) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (this is the key equilibrium step, exothermic, catalysed by V₂O₅ at ~450°C); (3) SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄ (in practice via oleum). The Contact process makes sulfuric acid.
items.explanation: Contact: S → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄. V₂O₅ catalyst. Exothermic at the equilibrium step.

items.question: What is the principal product of the OSTWALD process?
items.expectedAnswer: Nitric acid
items.explanation: Ostwald: NH₃ → NO → NO₂ → HNO₃ (nitric acid). Haber makes ammonia; Contact makes sulfuric acid; Ostwald makes nitric acid.

items.question: For the equilibrium CO(g) + 2H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g) (exothermic), predict the effect on the EQUILIBRIUM POSITION of: (a) adding more CO; (b) increasing pressure; (c) increasing temperature.
items.expectedAnswer: (a) Adding CO shifts equilibrium to the RIGHT (system uses up CO to oppose the addition); more CH₃OH forms. (b) Increasing pressure shifts to fewer gas moles: products (1 mol) < reactants (3 mol), so equilibrium shifts RIGHT; more CH₃OH. (c) Increasing temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction (forward is exothermic), so equilibrium shifts LEFT; less CH₃OH.
items.explanation: Three Le Chatelier applications in one. Concentration, pressure (gas moles), temperature (exothermic).

items.question: Why is a MODERATE TEMPERATURE chosen for the Haber process even though the forward reaction is exothermic and lower temperatures favour higher equilibrium yields?
items.expectedAnswer: Lower temperature gives higher equilibrium YIELD (favours exothermic forward direction) but lower RATE (kinetics slows). Higher temperature gives faster rate but lower yield. The choice of ~450°C is a COMPROMISE: high enough that the reaction proceeds at a useful industrial rate, low enough to keep yield reasonable. The catalyst (Fe) helps reach equilibrium faster at this moderate temperature.
items.explanation: Trade-off: yield vs rate. Catalyst helps with rate; moderate T balances both.

items.question: If an INERT GAS (e.g. He) is added at constant volume to the equilibrium N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, what happens to the equilibrium?
items.expectedAnswer: NO SHIFT. Adding an inert gas at CONSTANT VOLUME does not change the partial pressures (or concentrations) of N₂, H₂ or NH₃. The total pressure rises but the partial pressures (which appear in Kc) are unchanged. So Le Chatelier predicts no shift.
items.explanation: Inert gas at constant V: total P up, partial P unchanged ⇒ no shift. At constant P (where V expands to keep P fixed), partial pressures decrease ⇒ shift to more moles of gas. CAPS-level usually expects no-shift answer.

items.question: For 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) (Contact process, exothermic): how does INCREASING PRESSURE affect the yield?
items.expectedAnswer: Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward the side with FEWER moles of gas. Reactants: 2 + 1 = 3 mol. Products: 2 mol. So equilibrium shifts toward products ⇒ higher SO₃ yield. (However, in practice the Contact process uses moderate pressure because high pressure is expensive and the catalyst provides sufficient rate.)
items.explanation: Higher P ⇒ shift to fewer mol of gas. SO₃ side has fewer moles ⇒ yield ↑.

items.question: A learner says: 'In the Haber process, using a higher temperature increases the rate AND the yield.' Is this correct?
items.expectedAnswer: Partially correct. Higher T DOES increase the rate (kinetics: more particles have sufficient energy). But the Haber reaction is EXOTHERMIC, so higher T DECREASES the equilibrium yield (Le Chatelier: favours endothermic reverse). The learner has the kinetics right but the equilibrium wrong.
items.explanation: Kinetics vs equilibrium trade-off. Rate ↑, yield ↓ for exothermic at higher T.

items.question: For Co(H₂O)₆²⁺ (pink) ⇌ CoCl₄²⁻ (blue) + 6H₂O: how to shift the colour back from blue to pink?
items.expectedAnswer: Add water (dilute the solution)
items.explanation: Adding water (the product of the forward) shifts equilibrium back to reactants. Equivalently, decreasing [Cl⁻] (by dilution) drives equilibrium left ⇒ more pink Co(H₂O)₆²⁺.

items.question: If you DECREASE the volume of a sealed container containing the equilibrium 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), which way does the equilibrium shift and why?
items.expectedAnswer: Decreasing volume increases total pressure. By Le Chatelier, the equilibrium shifts to the side with FEWER moles of gas. Reactants: 2 mol NO₂; products: 1 mol N₂O₄. So equilibrium shifts to the RIGHT (toward N₂O₄). The dark brown NO₂ would diminish and the colourless N₂O₄ would increase.
items.explanation: Compress ⇒ pressure up ⇒ shift to fewer-mole side. NO₂ → N₂O₄ goes from 2 mol to 1 mol of gas.

items.question: Why is a CATALYST important in industrial equilibrium processes even though it doesn't shift the equilibrium?
items.expectedAnswer: A catalyst speeds the rate at which equilibrium is reached. Industrially, this means the desired equilibrium concentration is achieved in a much shorter time, making the process economically viable. Without the catalyst, low temperatures favourable for yield (in exothermic reactions) would give impractically slow rates.
items.explanation: Catalyst: time-to-equilibrium ↓. Without it, the trade-off between yield and rate forces unfavourable conditions.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_LECHATELIER_CONCENTRATION: Wrong shift direction for concentration change
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_LECHATELIER_TEMPERATURE: Wrong shift direction for temperature change (exo/endo confusion)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_LECHATELIER_PRESSURE: Wrong shift direction for pressure / volume change
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_KC_TEMPERATURE: Misjudges how T affects Kc for exo/endo
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_KC_ONLY_TEMPERATURE: Believes Kc changes with pressure or catalyst
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GAS_MOLES_COUNT: Wrong count of gas moles on each side
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_KINETICS_VS_EQUILIBRIUM: Confuses kinetic rate with equilibrium yield
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_INERT_GAS: Wrong shift prediction for inert gas addition
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_VOLUME_VS_PRESSURE: Wrong reasoning when changing volume vs pressure
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_CATALYST_INDUSTRY: Can't explain industrial role of catalyst
